comments.content: `SilentInstall.attempt` is called from inside `runCheck()`, so it runs while `runMutex.withLock` is still held. That means the worker's check lock stays held for the whole silent attempt: re-hashing the full APK, fetching the profile, waiting up to 15 s for `AuthManager`, then writing and committing the session. A concurrent periodic run or one-shot kick blocks on `runMutex` for all of that. It also means the process can be killed for the install while the worker is still running, before it returns `Result.success()`, so WorkManager may rerun the job. The comment says the attempt "never waits on this one". That's true for the attempt's own `tryLock`, but the reverse isn't: other check runs do wait on it. Consider releasing `runMutex` first. For example, have `runCheck()` return whether a valid pre-download exists, then call `SilentInstall.attempt` in `doWork()` after `withLock` returns.

The HTTP trust path can install code silently, so it needs a few adversarial cases that are missing now. Add tests for userinfo confusion (`http://10.0.2.2:8765@evil.com/k.apk`), which `java.net.URI` currently resolves to host `evil.com` and refuses. Also add a malformed or empty-host URL (`http://`, `http:///k.apk`) and a blank or whitespace-only `testBaseUrl`. These pin down today's correct behavior, so a later parser swap (e.g. to `Uri.parse` or string splitting) can't quietly weaken it.

If the tracker is not registered, this fails open. `register` can throw, and `PluginRuntimeHooks` swallows the error. When that happens, `log == null`, so `startedActivities` reads 0. `storeFor` then makes a new `PrefsVisibilityStore` whose `last_start`/`last_stop` are never written again in this process. `SilentInstallDecision.quiet` takes those stale or missing times as "out of sight since boot" and returns ELIGIBLE. The daily `UpdateCheckWorker` (`SilentTrigger.DAILY_CHECK`) still calls `SilentInstall.attempt`, so it can silently install over a member who is watching. Expose the registration state, e.g. `val isRegistered get() = log != null`, and have `SilentInstallGuard.quietInput` refuse when it is false (return `APP_ON_SCREEN` or a dedicated reason). Don't let an unknown state count as 0 started activities.

There's no test for an `https` test base URL, and `build.gradle.kts` accepts one (`scheme != "http" && scheme != "https"`). With `testBaseUrl = "https://10.0.2.2:8765"`, `isTrustedAssetUrl` currently trusts `http://10.0.2.2:8765/k.apk`, because it only checks host and port, not the test URL's scheme. So a server the developer set up as https can be served over plain http. Since this path can install silently, please add a test that pins the intended behavior (most likely: refuse the http asset). Either fix the implementation to compare schemes, or make the Gradle check accept only `http`.

comments.content: Two numeric edge cases that change how `SilentBlock.parse` behaves aren't covered: a number too big for a Long (e.g. `{"after": 99999999999999999999}`) and exponent notation (`{"after": 1.793e12}`). `longOrNull` returns null for both, so both become "no block" without any warning. That's probably fine for the overflow, but `release.sh` or a JSON tool could write a valid timestamp in exponent form, and silent install would then be turned off with no sign of it. Please add tests so this behavior is a deliberate, documented choice.

`holdsPrompt` hides the app-open prompt whenever a silent block exists, even if the silent path can't run for this version. The worst case is a missing pre-download. `shouldDownload` only downloads on an unmetered network, so a box on a metered or failing connection never gets the APK and `eligibility` keeps returning `NO_PREDOWNLOAD`, but the prompt stays hidden until `after + 72h`. If `after` is far in the future (or a typo), the prompt is hidden for that whole time. The same thing happens on a box that never goes quiet (the ambient screen), which goes against the non-goal that says such a box should get the prompt when someone uses it. Pass in whether a pre-download for `update.versionCode` exists and return false without one. Consider also limiting how long the hold can last before `after`.

comments.content: `SystemClock` is imported but never used in this file. Remove it.

This data class holds a lambda, so the generated `equals`/`hashCode` compare the function by identity. The early-user path in `SilentInstall.sequence` calls `copy(...)` and relies on the copy sharing the same lazy hash. That works today, but it's an easy contract to break by accident. Pass the checksum check to `eligibility` as its own parameter, or make this a plain class.

comments.content: The test name promises a 15 s wait, but nothing checks that the wait happened. The assertions would still pass if `signedInUserId` gave up on `Loading` straight away, or if `ACCOUNT_WAIT_MS` dropped to 0. Then a cold-process early user would never get the grace period meant for AuthManager to load. Under `runTest` the virtual clock moves forward by the timeout, so assert it.

comments.content: `FakeEnv` hardcodes `5_000_000L` and `1030`, copies of the outer `nowMs` and `live`. A nested class can't read them, so if someone edits the outer values, the fakes drift apart without any error. For example, tests that rely on `afterMs = nowMs + 1` would quietly change meaning. Move these into a `companion object` with `const val`s and use them in both places. Also, `var quiet` is never reassigned, so it can be a `val`.

comments.content: If the check fails, this treats external playback as not running. For a guard whose job is to keep a silent install away from a member who is watching something, it should fail closed. If `getRunningServices` throws (a `SecurityException`, an OEM quirk), the silent install can restart the app in the middle of external playback. Return `true` here so the attempt is skipped and tried again on the next trigger. Logging the failure would also help.

The script only looks for `--no-silent` in the first argument. Silent install is now the default, so this mistake fails open. `./release.sh 0.7.5-beta --no-silent "notes"` publishes a release that installs silently on every box after 24 h, and the notes text becomes `--no-silent notes`. A typo such as `--no-silnet` is taken as the versionName and gets written into build.gradle.kts. Since a committed silent install can't be undone, reject any versionName that starts with `-`, and either reject `--no-silent` anywhere after the version or remove it from the notes and honour it.

comments.content: `FakeEnv` hardcodes `predownloadPath`, `fileExists` and `sha256Matches` to success, so no test can reach `SilentInstall.sequence`'s pre-download wiring: `cachedFileExists = path != null && env.fileExists(path)` and the lazy `shaMatches` that checks `path != null && update != null`. If that wiring broke (for example, `cachedFileExists` ignored a null path, or the sha result was flipped), a corrupt or missing APK could reach `openSession`, and every test here would still pass. The decision tests only check the pure function, not how `run` builds its input. Make these overridable (`var fileExists = true`, `var shaMatches = true`, `var path: String? = ...`). Then add `run`-level cases that assert `NO_PREDOWNLOAD` and `PREDOWNLOAD_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` and check that no session calls happen.

comments.content: `holdsPrompt` uses `nowMs - afterMs < SAFETY_NET_MS` so the check can't overflow. That's the reason it doesn't write `nowMs < afterMs + SAFETY_NET_MS`. No test pins this: a very large `after` from the manifest (for example, `Long.MAX_VALUE`) isn't covered. If someone "simplifies" it back to the addition form, `afterMs + SAFETY_NET_MS` wraps negative and the prompt is never held, and the tests stay green. Add a case with `update(silentAfterMs = Long.MAX_VALUE)` that asserts `holds(...)` is true.

comments.content: Dead code: nothing calls `AppVisibilityTracker.lastStartElapsedMs(context)` or `lastStopElapsedMs(context)`. `SilentInstallGuard.buildQuietInput` reads the keys straight from `storeFor(context)`. The same is true of `VisibilityLog.lastStartElapsedMs()`/`lastStopElapsedMs()`, which only tests call. That leaves two read paths for the same data that can drift apart. Either remove these, or have `SilentInstallGuard` use them so there is only one path.
